sections.content:
20,685 people

were counted on the census as "managers in logistics" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Managers in logistics plan and co-ordinate the supply chain of goods and services between the point of production and consumption, including their efficient transportation, storage and retailing.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "managers in logistics", 14.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "managers in logistics" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "managers in logistics" included:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • IT project managers
  • business and financial project management professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "managers in logistics" there were more men than women (72.2% compared with 27.8%).

This means "managers in logistics" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 72.2% and women made up 27.8% of "managers in logistics"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "managers in logistics" included:

  • pre-press technicians
  • musicians
  • managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "managers in logistics" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "managers in logistics" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "managers in logistics", 5.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (94.9% compared with 5.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.2%) than self-employed (4.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
